The `_canReuseMaterialized` fast path vs. rebuild-only split (contract item a), read directly off the per-layer loop body (lines 4762-4796): steps shared by BOTH paths for a given layer are the `dupOnly` skip test (4763), the effective-visibility empty/continue branch (4764, its own separate early exit — a layer that fails this never reaches the reuse test at all), and resolving `strokes=getEffectiveStrokesRendered(i,idx)` (4783). Outside the per-layer loop entirely (lines 4797-4828), and therefore UNCONDITIONAL regardless of which path any individual layer took: `applyElemVisibilityAll()` (4800, re-derives element-level visibility for every layer every load, cheap enough that it was never worth gating), `userLayers[state.activeLayerIdx].activate()` (4801), the `selectedPaths` re-resolution block (4810-4823), and `SMCamera.applyCameraView()` (4828). `saveActiveLayerFrameOrPromote`'s promotion rule (contract item c) is structurally DIFFERENT from `_maybePromoteInterpolated` (C21o), despite both existing to turn an interpolated/held frame into a real keyframe on a genuine edit: `_maybePromoteInterpolated` (C21o, app.js:4597-4599) is a passive, content-diff-gated check invoked FROM INSIDE `saveActiveLayerFrame`/`saveAllLayerFrames` on every save, requiring BOTH `window._tweenFrameDirty` AND a `strokesEqual` mismatch before flipping `f.isKeyframe=true;f.isInterpolated=false` — it never runs on a genuinely HELD (non-keyframe, non-interpolated) frame at all, because those saves already early-return before reaching it (C21o's own gate at app.js:4688/4706). `saveActiveLayerFrameOrPromote` (this scope) is the function that handles the HELD-frame case those early-returns create: called explicitly by a caller that wants to guarantee SOME write lands even on a hold (`if(!f||f.isKeyframe||f.isInterpolated){saveActiveLayerFrame();return;}` at line 4971 delegates the keyframe/interpolated case straight to the ordinary save — `_maybePromoteInterpolated` still applies there, unchanged), but for a genuinely held frame it takes ONE of two mode-specific actions instead: in Animation 2D (`state.appMode!=='motion'`), it unconditionally promotes the CURRENT frame itself to a real keyframe (`f.isKeyframe=true;f.isInterpolated=false`, line 4974) — no content-diff gate at all, promotion happens on every call regardless of whether anything actually changed, because the function's own callers (tools.js flip/align/distribute/boolean-op, timeline.js flip) are only ever invoked as the DIRECT result of a real edit gesture; in Motion, it instead walks BACKWARD to the hold's own origin keyframe (`for(var o=state.currentFrame;o>=0;o--)`, lines 4981-4987) and overwrites THAT frame's `strokes` directly via `_collectLayerStrokes`, never minting a new keyframe at the current frame — consistent with Motion's own semantics where a hold's whole duration belongs to one keyframe. `saveActiveLayerFrameOrPromote` itself calls NO `pushUndo`/`pushUndoLayers` of any kind (confirmed by a line-by-line read of its own body) — unlike `setElemHidden` (this scope, which calls `pushUndoLayers()` directly), its own callers (tools.js:1321/1365/1645/6031, confirmed by reading tools.js:1319 immediately before the first call site: `if(!moved){state.undoStack.pop();return;}`, evidence that the undo snapshot was already captured earlier in the SAME gesture) are expected to have already pushed undo themselves before the gesture completes.

`saveActiveLayerFrameOrPromote` is the SECOND producer of `_justEnsuredKeyframeAt` (contract item c cross-reference) — alongside `ensureKeyframe` (tools.js:1882, C21o's own citation), this scope's own line 4974 sets `ld._justEnsuredKeyframeAt=state.currentFrame` immediately before calling `saveActiveLayerFrame()` (line 4975) for the IDENTICAL reason: C21o's own trim-range gate (app.js:4685) would otherwise reject the very save meant to persist a frame that was JUST promoted from a hold to a keyframe, if that frame happens to sit outside the layer's own in/out trim range. A whole-src grep of `_justEnsuredKeyframeAt` confirms exactly these two producers and one consumer (C21o's `saveActiveLayerFrame`, app.js:4683-4684) exist anywhere in the codebase.

`syncLinkedKeyframeFolder` (contract item d) copies ONLY keyframe TIMING, never `strokes` content, between siblings in the same `state.layerLinkGroups[gid].linkedKeyframes` group — confirmed by direct read of its own body (lines 5014-5022): when the source frame IS a keyframe and the sibling's frame is NOT, it sets `f.isKeyframe=true;f.isInterpolated=false` and only initializes `f.strokes=[]` IF THE SIBLING FRAME HAD NO STROKES ARRAY AT ALL (`if(!f.strokes)f.strokes=[]`) — never overwriting an existing array with the source's own content.
